title: Changing the common base of two flat families gives a Tor-independent square
statement:
Let $S$ be any scheme and let $X\to S$ and $Y\to S$ be flat morphisms [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be any $S$-morphism, let $a:S'\to S$ be arbitrary, and form $Y'=Y\times_SS'$ and $X'=X\times_SS'\simeq X\times_YY'$ with projections $b:Y'\to Y$ and $a_X:X'\to X$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then $f$ and $b$ are Tor independent in the stalkwise sense of [def-pc-pullback-stalk-tensor-comparison]: for every $x\in X$ and $y'\in Y'$ with common image $y\in Y$, and every integer $i>0$,
$$\operatorname{Tor}^{\mathcal O_{Y,y}}_i(\mathcal O_{X,x},\mathcal O_{Y',y'})=0.$$
Here Tor is computed by a projective resolution [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. No flatness of $f$ or $a$, no properness, no finiteness and no reducedness of the base are required.

proof.text: Fix $x\in X$ and $y'\in Y'$ over the same $y\in Y$, and let $s\in S$, $s'\in S'$ be their images. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], choose $W=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$ around $s$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset Y$ around $y$ mapping into $W$, $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset X$ around $x$ mapping into $V$, and $W'=\operatorname{Spec}C\subset S'$ around $s'$ mapping into $W$. Put $E=A\otimes_R C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $V\times_W W'=\operatorname{Spec}E$ is an open neighbourhood of $y'$ in $Y'$. The stalk identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-stalk-localization] identify the structural stalk maps with localized ring maps. Flatness of $X\to S$ and $Y\to S$ in [def-weil-flat-morphism] therefore says, at every prime of $B$ and $A$, that the corresponding localization is flat over the base localization. Apply [lem-pc-affine-sections-flat-over-base], first to $B$ and then to $A$ as modules over themselves, to conclude that both are flat over $R$.

Choose an augmented free $R$-module resolution $P_\bullet\to C$ as in [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. Since $A$ is $R$-flat, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] makes $A\otimes_R P_\bullet\to E$ exact. It is a free $A$-resolution: if $P_n$ has basis $(e_j)$, the maps $a\otimes\sum_j r_je_j\mapsto(ar_j)_j$ and $(a_j)_j\mapsto\sum_j a_j\otimes e_j$ identify $A\otimes_RP_n$ with the free $A$-module on that basis. Tensor this resolution over $A$ with $B$. In every degree the mutually inverse formulas $(a\otimes p)\otimes b\mapsto p\otimes ab$ and $p\otimes b\mapsto(1\otimes p)\otimes b$ give $(A\otimes_RP_n)\otimes_AB\cong P_n\otimes_RB$ and commute with the differentials. The latter augmented complex is exact by $R$-flatness of $B$ and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact]. Thus the resolution definition gives $\operatorname{Tor}^A_i(E,B)=0$ for every $i>0$, and [lem-weil-pbc-tor-symmetry] gives $\operatorname{Tor}^A_i(B,E)=0$.

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak p\subset B$, $\mathfrak q\subset A$, and $\mathfrak r\subset E$ represent $x,y,y'$. The contractions of $\mathfrak p$ and $\mathfrak r$ to $A$ are both $\mathfrak q$. For each $i>0$, [lem-pc-tor-vanishing-localized-algebra], with base $A$, coefficient algebra $B$, multiplicative set $B\setminus\mathfrak p$, and other module $E$, gives $\operatorname{Tor}^A_i(B_{\mathfrak p},E)=0$. Apply [lem-trf-tor-localization-on-spec] with base $A$, module $B_{\mathfrak p}$, algebra $E$ and prime $\mathfrak r$; its isomorphism identifies $\operatorname{Tor}^A_i(B_{\mathfrak p},E_{\mathfrak r})$ with the localization of this zero module. Both modules are $A_{\mathfrak q}$-modules: an element outside $\mathfrak q$ maps outside $\mathfrak p$ and $\mathfrak r$ and hence becomes a unit in each localization. With these actions, [lem-pc-tor-vanishing-localized-base] applied to $A\to A_{\mathfrak q}$ yields $\operatorname{Tor}^{A_{\mathfrak q}}_i(B_{\mathfrak p},E_{\mathfrak r})=0$.

source.place: Tag 0B67 (lemma-tor-amplitude-localization), source and base localization; algebra.tex Tag 00M8 (lemma-flat-base-change-tor), free-resolution argument for coefficient localization.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] the three local rings just used are $\mathcal O_{X,x}=B_{\mathfrak p}$, $\mathcal O_{Y,y}=A_{\mathfrak q}$ and $\mathcal O_{Y',y'}=E_{\mathfrak r}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-stalk-localization], their module actions are exactly the stalk maps of $f$ and $b$. Since the pair $(x,y')$ was arbitrary, step 3 is precisely the vanishing for every pair required by [def-pc-pullback-stalk-tensor-comparison]. Finally, [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $X\times_SS'$ with $X\times_Y(Y\times_SS')$: a map to either side is a pair of maps to $X,S'$ with equal composites to $S$, the map to $Y$ being forced to be the composite with $f$. The inverse identifications preserve projections by uniqueness in that universal property. All arguments were local at the chosen pair, so empty schemes impose no extra case and no finiteness, properness or reducedness was used.
